subject.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue

question: Should maintainers adopt the owner-first durable boundary in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107375 and require this PR’s queue-handoff work to be recreated as a narrow, generation-fenced successor, or retain this cumulative branch as the implementation candidate?
rationale: The branch changes shared durable storage and session-delivery semantics, while the documented replacement is intentionally only an RFC; source-level repair cannot choose the canonical owner, public surface, or reset policy.

options.title: Adopt owner-first successor
options.body: Accept the RFC boundary, keep this PR as evidence only, and request a narrow successor that restores the handoff with default session-generation fencing.

options.title: Continue this branch
options.body: Designate this cumulative branch as the canonical implementation candidate and resolve its SQLite, protocol, and reset-policy boundaries before merge.

options.title: Reject shared durable layer
options.body: Reject the residual durable layer and retain only owner-specific changes inside existing session, task, flow, and delivery owners.

recommendation.title: Adopt owner-first successor
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC boundary, keep this PR as evidence only, and request a narrow successor that restores the handoff with default session-generation fencing.

likelyOwner.reason: The author documented both the original implementation boundary and the proposed owner-first replacement decision in the linked RFC.
